prompts.original:
You manage one position in a four-role Beer Game: retailer, wholesaler,
distributor and factory. Minimize total TEAM inventory holding plus backlog costs
across weeks. Each unit left in stock costs 0.50 per week; each unit still backlogged
costs 1.00 per week. There is no sales revenue, order-placement charge, bulk discount
or reward for a large order. Shipments automatically fill owed demand when stock exists.
Your only choice is the integer number of cases to order upstream (factory: produce).
Orders must be nonnegative. Zero is a legitimate choice when justified by the state;
it is not a default. No preferred order, target beta or expected treatment effect exists.

The current observation is AFTER deliveries and shipments and BEFORE your order.
Current cost is already incurred; your order affects later weeks, not today's cost.
Unfilled demand is backlogged rather than lost. Orders cannot be canceled. An order
travels upstream in one week, actual shipments take two weeks downstream, and factory
production takes three weeks. Supplier shortages can further delay replenishment.
Inventory is available stock. Supply_line is all your previous orders not yet received,
including goods in transit and orders waiting upstream; it is not immediately usable stock.

All roles share their current physical inventories, shown in shared_inventory. You know
your own demand, inventory, backlog, supply line and history. Other roles' orders,
backlogs and outstanding orders are not revealed. No inter-agent communication is allowed.
Initial stock is 12 per role and initial flow 4 per week. First four weeks use fixed
orders of 4 for familiarization. Future customer demand and last decision week are unknown.
After decisions stop, 12 automatically scored weeks carry all stock/backlog/pipeline
forward; customer demand stays at its last value, and each role automatically orders
its incoming demand. This continuation policy is only for terminal evaluation, not a
recommended strategy for your choices. Minimize team costs across both phases.
Respond to the current task using the provided observations; do not imitate a human
stereotype or try to create oscillations. No external tools are available.

Respond to the current task using the provided observations; do not imitate a human
stereotype or try to create oscillations. No external tools are available.
Physical rules, applying in every round:
Demand is the NEW incoming order processed this week. Backlog is the TOTAL still
unfilled after this week's shipments, including any unfilled part of that demand.
Backlog remains owed, even when next week's new demand is zero. It incurs cost
each week until goods actually fill it. It is not canceled by a quiet week.
For the FACTORY, your order directly starts production now. There is no outside
supplier, raw-material constraint or production-capacity constraint. A production
order q placed in week t becomes available factory stock in week t+3. It does not
require an existing supply line to start, and no extra order-transmission or
downstream-shipping lag is added before that production becomes your own stock.
For the other roles, orders go to the immediate upstream role; stock shortages
there may delay shipment. Supply_line includes previous orders still unreceived;
these remain active commitments. Your action can affect future holding/backlog
costs even though it cannot change the already-processed current week.
No ordering formula or preferred quantity is supplied. Choose using the stated
team objective over future weeks as well as the automatic continuation.

quiz.task: Check physical game rules, not an ordering strategy.

questions.factory_production_receipt_week: The factory starts producing 6 cases in week 10. Which week does this production become available factory stock?
questions.production_requires_existing_supply_line: Must the factory already have something in its supply line before it can start new production?
questions.backlog_next_week_without_receipts: A role ends this week with inventory 0 and backlog 20. Next week it receives no goods and no new demand. What is its ending backlog?
questions.next_week_backlog_cost: In that same next week, what is the backlog cost?
questions.zero_new_demand_cancels_backlog: Does zero new demand cancel previously unfilled orders?
questions.current_backlog_already_includes_unfille: In the supplied after-shipments observation, does backlog already include the unfilled portion of this week’s demand?

retries: transport only, at most two retries; no correctness retries
eligibility: Adequate allowance: positive production in all four empty-pipeline factory shortage cases
No order above the existing emergency threshold
selection: Among eligible models choose lowest input/output prices; within model prefer clarified if eligible. Never select on H1/H2 direction or significance.
limitations: Development states include failures selected from pilot 02; not a generalization test. Short shortage behavior is reported but does not determine selection. No game p-values.
